questions.text:
1. Explain the Problem or Situation

Describe the authentic context that creates a need for a technological outcome. Explain the problem, issue, opportunity, or situation and why an outcome is required for the end user(s).

Think about:

  • What is happening in the situation?
  • What problem needs solving?
  • Why is a new or improved outcome needed?
questions.hint: To score highly, clearly explain the REAL situation the end user faces. Describe the problem, why it matters, and what makes the context authentic (where, when, why).

rubric.check: why|because|so that|in order to|so they can|so it can|so I can|so we can
environment|setting|where|location|space|area|at home|at school|in the classroom|in the workshop|outside|outdoors|indoors

questions.text:
2. Create a Technological Brief

A brief is a statement of intent that identifies:

  • The purpose of the outcome
  • The end user(s)
  • The intended environment where it will be used

Write a clear brief that explains the technological intent of your proposed outcome.
questions.hint: Mention the purpose, the specific end user, and the exact environment where the outcome will be used. Use formal technological language like 'statement of intent' and 'fitness for purpose'.

questions.text:
3. Write the Specifications

Specifications are short, precise, measurable statements describing what the outcome must be or do.

You must include:

  • Physical requirements (materials, size, durability, safety, construction)
  • Functional requirements (what it must do, how it must perform)

Write at least 6–10 measurable specifications.
questions.hint: High-scoring specs are measurable (e.g., dimensions, weight limits, materials). Avoid vague words like ‘nice’ or ‘good’. Use numbers, tolerances, materials, and performance verbs.

questions.text:
4. Evaluate the Specifications

Explain whether each specification was met or not met, and justify your judgement.

You must:

  • Refer to evidence (measurements, testing, user feedback)
  • Explain why each specification was met or not met
  • Discuss fitness for purpose in the end user’s environment
questions.hint: To achieve Excellence, link your judgement to clear evidence (testing, measurements, user feedback). Explain WHY it was met/not met and discuss fitness for purpose in the real environment.
